claims.evidence: Photo 0 clearly shows an 'LG' logo on the upper left of the unit, not Samsung.

claims.claim: LG Washing machine scrap but doesn't work and needs repair
claims.evidence: No power-on test, error code screen, or drum movement is shown; condition claim cannot be confirmed from a single static photo.

risks.risk: Functional state (does it power on, spin, heat, dry) is unknown
risks.proof: Video of unit plugged in, powering on, and completing a short spin/dry cycle

risks.risk: Drum, door seal, and hose condition unseen
risks.proof: Close-up photos of drum interior, rubber door seal, and inlet/outlet hoses

risks.risk: Internal electronics/control board condition and error history unknown
risks.proof: Photo/video of display showing any stored error codes, or technician diagnostic report

risks.risk: Accessories (hoses, manual, power cord condition) completeness unknown
risks.proof: Photo of all included accessories laid out together

risks.risk: Core brand/identity mismatch between seller's claim (Samsung) and witness-confirmed LG labeling suggests possible photo mix-up or misrepresentation
risks.proof: Clear, dated photo of the model/serial plate and brand logo together with the item in current location
risks.if_unproven: treated as unresolved identity conflict, blocking any firm valuation

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the brand logo and model/serial plate together in one frame
Video of the unit being powered on and attempting a cycle
Timestamped or dated photo to confirm this is the actual item being sold, matching the witness's photo
Close-up of drum interior, door seal, and hose connections
Photo of any accessories included (hoses, manual, cord)
response.reason: The seller's claim of 'Samsung' directly contradicts the witness-confirmed LG branding on the unit, a core identity fact that should never be in dispute, raising concern about photo substitution or misrepresentation before any price can be set.
